abstract: PURPOSE: High-dose chemotherapy (HD-Ctx) followed by autologous peripheral-blood stem-cell (PBSC) transplantation is currently investigated in patients with poor prognosis or relapsed metastatic germ cell tumor (GCTs). This study analyzed the presence and the clinical importance of contaminating tumor cells in PBSC preparations used to support HD-Ctx in GCT patients. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Seven targets for reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR)-based detection of GCT cells were able to detect seminomatous and different histologic variants of nonseminomatous tumor cells. PBSC preparations from 57 patients were investigated for the presence of contaminating tumor cells using this set of targets, including beta human chorionic gonadotropin (beta-hCG), fibronectin (EDB variant), epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), CD44 (v8 to 10 variant), germ cell and placental alkaline phosphatase (AP), human endogenous retrovirus type K (ENV and GAG), and XIST. Samples of PBSC preparations from four healthy donors for allogenic transplantations as well as blood specimens from 10 healthy volunteers served as negative controls. RESULTS: Fifty patients (43 first-line and seven second-line Ctx) were assessable. Combining all RT-PCR results, 29 PBSC preparations (58%) were positive for tumor-specific amplification products (HERV-K 0, fibronectin 4, XIST 14, beta-hCG 19, AP 19, CD44 24, EGFR 26). Ten (35%) of 29 patients who underwent transplantation with positive PBSC preparations and seven (33%) of 21 patients with negative PBSC preparations have suffered relapse or progression (not significant [ns]). With a median follow-up of 22 months (2 to 66) post-HD-Ctx projected 3-year survival rates are 68% (RT-PCR+) and 58% (RT-PCR-) (ns). None of the 10 control peripheral-blood samples showed positivity for any of the targets studied. CONCLUSION: GCT cells can be detected in more than 50% of PBSC preparations using a RT-PCR approach with multiple targets. Despite the presence of tumor cells, retransplantation of the PBSC products did not effect long-term outcome. Factors such as responsiveness to chemotherapy and tumor mass seem to overcome the importance of potentially re-infused tumor cells.
abstract_ja: 目的: 再発または予後不良の転移性胚細胞腫瘍に対し、自家末梢血幹細胞(PBSC)移植を伴う大量化学療法(HD-Ctx)が検討されている。本研究では、HD-Ctxを支持するPBSC製剤中の混入腫瘍細胞の有無と臨床的意義を解析した。患者と方法: セミノーマおよび非セミノーマの各組織型の腫瘍細胞を検出できる7種類の標的を用いてRT-PCR法を行い、57例のPBSC製剤を解析した。同種移植のための健常ドナー4例のPBSC製剤および健常ボランティア10例の血液検体を陰性対照とした。結果: 50例(初回化学療法43例、二次化学療法7例)が評価可能であった。RT-PCRの全結果を統合すると、29製剤(58%)が腫瘍特異的増幅産物陽性であった(HERV-K 0、フィブロネクチン4、XIST 14、β-hCG 19、AP 19、CD44 24、EGFR 26)。陽性PBSC製剤で移植を受けた29例中10例(35%)、陰性製剤の21例中7例(33%)が再発または進行を経験した(有意差なし)。HD-Ctx後の中央追跡期間22か月(2~66)における3年生存率は、RT-PCR陽性で68%、陰性で58%であった(有意差なし)。対照の末梢血10検体はいずれの標的も陽性とならなかった。結論: 多標的RT-PCR法により、胚細胞腫瘍細胞はPBSC製剤の50%以上で検出可能であった。腫瘍細胞が存在したにもかかわらず、PBSC製剤の再輸注は長期転帰に影響しなかった。化学療法への反応性や腫瘍量が、再輸注される腫瘍細胞の影響を上回るようである。
